answer: Each identity claims one basalt parcel in a registry and locks a 90-credit bond. A surveyor fires a pulse into the parcel and records its echo and karst cavity map; the registry rejects any claim with a matching echo. The k-th survey fee is 110+15(k-1) credits, so 1,000 fakes pay 7,602,500 in fees plus 90,000 in bonds. A rented parcel ring fails: a rented plot's echo is registered, and the duplicate claim burns its bond. Auditors re-fire the pulse to check signatures; a mismatch burns the bond. An honest agent claims one parcel, pays 110 once, and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
